findings.summary: The list holds one hand-picked name and the sync test checks only one direction, so this fixes the Hermes instance, not the class.
findings.evidence: docs/ontology.toml has 7 terms (planning, job, Athena, Hermes, product versus system, landed, Sri), and each has a `misread` and `senses` field. Its own rule says a term is added only when it causes a misread. So the plan's criterion for choosing Hermes ('the one ontology term whose second sense caused a reading misread') is a judgment made once, and it is not recorded per term. The planned test only fails when a listed name is missing from the ontology. A term added to the ontology after a future misread passes every test and is never gated, which is the same gap that let 0wtc through. The plan's mitigation is a prose sentence in D165, which goes against the 'mechanism' default. Fix: Make the sync test check both directions. Add a private `UNGATED_TERMS` constant in reading.rs listing each other ontology term with a short reason (for example `job`, `planning` and `landed` are common words, `Athena` is in nearly every request, `Sri` is a name convention). Assert that every `[[term]]` name in docs/ontology.toml is in exactly one of AMBIGUOUS_NAMES or UNGATED_TERMS, and keep the Zeus control for the existing direction. Then adding an ontology term fails the build until someone decides whether readings must define it. This touches no file the reading puts out of scope.

findings.summary: The gate makes the reading restate Hermes but does not tie the restatement to the recorded senses, so the exact 0wtc misread (taking one sense as the whole) still passes.
findings.evidence: `defined_terms` accepts any `Term x:` line with three or more words of meaning. For example, `Term Hermes: the studied self-improving agent` (the plan's own accepted example) names only sense (1), while docs/ontology.toml:86-89 records two senses. The error only says to cite docs/ontology.toml 'if there is one'. Fix: For names on AMBIGUOUS_NAMES, accept the `Term` line only if it cites `docs/ontology.toml` (or, at minimum, make the error tell the reader to say which recorded sense applies and to cite the file). Add one refusing case for a Hermes definition without the citation. Alternatively, state this limit in the doc comment and in D165.

findings.summary: The Unreleased section would hold both 'check_defined_terms covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs' and 'covers 2 of the 3', plus an 'are not caught' sentence that is no longer true.
findings.evidence: CHANGELOG.md:22 says 'check_defined_terms covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs' and CHANGELOG.md:114-116 says the other two jobs 'are not caught'. Both sit under `## [Unreleased]` (line 8), so they are not released history. The append-only drift rule in send_back.rs covers docs/decisions.md, not CHANGELOG.md. The plan keeps these lines only so the existing tests keep their needles. Fix: Because the old bullets are unreleased, update them in place and move the needles in `delivery_verb_replay_over_the_cited_jobs` and `defined_terms_replay_over_the_cited_jobs` to the new wording. If they must stay, change nothing else but have the new bullet name the stale lines it supersedes. Leave D164 untouched either way.

findings.summary: The planned replacement produces a redundant sentence.
findings.evidence: reading.rs:3662 reads '[`check_defined_terms`] catches the first of them, and no check catches the second'. Replacing only the last clause with 'and `check_defined_terms` catches both of them' gives 'check_defined_terms catches the first of them, and check_defined_terms catches both of them'. Fix: Rewrite the whole clause as '[`check_defined_terms`] catches both of them', keeping the needles `covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs`, `outside the check` and `check_defined_terms`.

findings.summary: The pre-change failure is argued from the code, not observed.
findings.evidence: Step 6 says 'Check the pre-change failure by reasoning from the code'. The reasoning is right: before the change, structural_term never matches 'hermes', so check_defined_terms returns Ok. But nothing is run to show it. Fix: Have the producer add the new tests first, run `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` against the unchanged reading.rs, record the failing test names, then make the change.

summary: I read reading.rs (STRUCTURAL_TERMS at 3724, structural_term at 3886, defined_terms, check_defined_terms at 3909-3959, request_words, the plain-prose filters and the doc and share tests at 10790-10932), refusal_corpus.rs (CITED_REQUESTS at 478-489, the two replay tests, defined_terms_decision_and_changelog, INPUT_FORMS of 38), docs/ontology.toml, CHANGELOG.md and the append-only rule in send_back.rs and plan.rs. Every function, line and helper the plan cites exists. The recorded 0wtc request contains "Hermes Agent" in plain prose, so the extended matcher would catch it. request_words lowercases words and keeps `'s`, so the canonical-name and possessive design works. The dependents list matches the readers I found: no other request text in crates/ contains Hermes. The demonstrations use the real `refusing_check` and `check_defined_terms`, and each would fail before the change. One soundness problem should be fixed before code is written. The ambiguous-name list is a hand-picked constant with a single entry, and the drift test only checks one direction. So a new ontology term that causes a misread is never gated unless someone remembers to add it. That keeps the 'whole class' claim resting on prose, not on a mechanism. The other findings are minor: a gated definition can still repeat the 0wtc misread, the Unreleased changelog would state two conflicting counts, and one doc sentence would read awkwardly.
